At O(a^2), C0*theta_dot+H*theta=q_r4(t), and the measured bath heat is H*theta. Its complex 2*omega component is q_r4,2/[1-i*2*omega*C0/H], while the mean is unchanged.

finite_amplitude_closure_outline.status: Analytical new-apparatus construction only; numerical domain, stability, signal margin, runtime and model difficulty unestablished.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.material: Retain k(T)=k0*[1+g*(T-T0)/T0], g=.5, only within the measured [.9*T0,1.1*T0] neighborhood. Specify known positive fixed-extension heat capacity C0, constant kappa, and one locally equilibrated temperature for the whole spring-dashpot contact. There is no unknown caloric coefficient.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.thermal_apparatus: At each face replace the ideal clamp by a known positive conductance H to its own fixed-T0 bath. The whole contact is otherwise thermally isolated, including from the fluid and the other contact. Bulk fluid dissipation is collected separately by a prescribed T0 bulk thermostat; material gamma, nu and rho remain specified constants. The front detector reads H*(T_front-T0), with the original incident clock and explicit normalization. Define rho itself or C0/rho and H/rho in the same mechanical units.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.preparation_and_drive: Use a specified finite incident amplitude and the attracting periodic state, or a fully stated finite-time preparation if that state is not unique. The validity of the selected branch and temperature neighborhood must be checked. The current linear transverse idealization must be explicitly retained as a one-dimensional incompressible model: v=v_y(z,t), so advective transverse acceleration vanishes; pressure/normal constraints balance normal magnetic forces without normal work. Do not silently extrapolate an unspecified weak-field bulk model.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.source: A completed one-way approximation solves the correct cold Maxwell-fluid/contact response at T0, then evolves the stated thermal balance with that e(t),v_d(t), including the full T*k_prime*e*e_dot term and dissipation. The physical model instead solves the thermal state and k(T)-dependent traction together with the Maxwell-fluid boundary problem. It must preserve the same material, unknown p and detector; source and oracle differ only in this one-way mechanical approximation.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.calibration: Measure the weak-drive normalized mean coefficient, as already operationally defined in r4. Both models share it exactly for every p because the missing mechanical feedback begins at O(a^3), giving an O(a^4) heat correction. The nonzero weak-limit coefficient retains the inherited p information. Finite-amplitude mean readings are generally not an exactly shared calibration and cannot be represented as such. Any inherited records and noise draws would have to be explicitly identified as reused.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.distinction_from_prior_repairs: The source already uses the correct r4 reversible heat, finite thermal storage and both contact/field dynamics in the cold limit. It does not omit the positive internal heating term of the earlier finite-amplitude rod outline. The proposed failure is treating a locally heated constitutive boundary as a one-way output despite its k(T) changing the fields that heat it.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.margin_qualification: Within the measured temperature neighborhood, abs(delta k)/k0 is at most .05. This does not imply a .04 observable margin in either direction. Feedback can be weak, and temperature/harmonic cancellations or unstable branches may spoil a usable benchmark. No clock, amplitude, conductance or response point was chosen numerically here.
finite_amplitude_closure_outline.independent_reference: A time-domain Maxwell/current spatial discretization coupled to separate contact internal-energy or entropy variables, evaluating front bath flux directly, could be compared with an independently constructed harmonic-balance/periodic-orbit solver. Time, spatial and harmonic truncations must be independently refined. Global averaged incoming-minus-outgoing optical power must balance bulk and both measured bath heats; transient energy and local entropy balances must also close. Merely attaching the same heat-transfer factor to both codes is not an independent feedback reference.
